function: Learned construction of a differentiable channel knowledge map: a BPNN estimates the location-dependent large-scale channel power gain towards each GBS, migrated to nearby GBSs by transfer learning (pp. 3-6).
system: K UAVs at 50 m uplink to ground BSs; scalar channel power gain, no antennas or RIS stated (effectively single-antenna); 180 kHz bandwidth, band not stated (pp. 3, 10-11).
method: Feedforward BPNN (tanh and linear hidden layers, 40 neurons each), supervised Levenberg-Marquardt training on MSE; transfer learning freezes the first hidden layer, retrains the rest (pp. 4-6, 10).
data_channel: Public radio map dataset of central Shanghai (github.com/6wj/radiomap-uav, [24]), described as measured channel gains on a 94x94 grid at 50 m; used for training and testing (p. 10).
test_conditions: GBS 1 CKM trained on 2000 samples (counts swept), tested on full ground-truth map; transferred to GBSs 2-6 with 800 samples; optimization with 2, 3, 5 UAVs (pp. 10-15).
baselines: CKM: KNN [15] and Kriging [19] interpolation, Unet [25], fresh training; trajectory and power: LoS-model alternating optimization [8], grid-quantization CKM path planning with fixed power [28] (pp. 10-12).
metrics: MAE of channel gain (dB), CKM construction time, minimal average rate and per-UAV rates (bps/Hz), convergence, rate versus maximum power and dmin (pp. 11-15).
complexity: Measured CKM construction (training) time versus number of samples (Fig. 6(b)); optimization Algorithm 2 complexity O(L N^(7/2) K^7) (pp. 10-11).
openness: No own code released; trains and tests on the public dataset https://github.com/6wj/radiomap-uav, with 3D city map from https://www.openstreetmap.org (p. 10).
q1_support: p. 2: "trained and tested by an open dataset for the radio map of the Shanghai Central"; p. 10: "form the measured channel data" and "The datasets used in this paper are from the available datasets at https://github.com/6wj/radiomap-uav". Public dataset [24], not a custom simulator; reviewer to confirm measured versus ray-traced.
q2_support: p. 11: "we only choose N2 = 800 samples to construct CKM G2 of GBS 2"; p. 11: "the MAEs of migrated CKMs are consistently lower than those of freshly trained CKMs" (GBS 1 network transferred to new GBS sites 2-6 by freezing its first hidden layer and retraining the rest).
q3_support: p. 10: "Kriging-based CKM [19]" and "Unet-based CKM [25]"; p. 11: "Fig. 6(a) shows that MAEs of the four schemes versus different numbers of samples" (non-learned Kriging and KNN interpolation and the earlier learned Unet [25], all compared on MAE).
q4_support: p. 11: "Fig. 6(b) illustrates the training time of the four schemes" (time of constructing the CKM in seconds); p. 10: "the overall complexity of Algorithm 2, by retaining only the highest order term, is" O(LN^(7/2)K^7).
q5_support: p. 10: "The datasets used in this paper are from the available datasets at https://github.com/6wj/radiomap-uav" (public channel-gain dataset used for training and testing; no code of its own is released).
notes: Include, area 2. The learned component is the BPNN-based differentiable CKM with transfer-learning migration; it estimates the large-scale channel power gain at any UAV location (p. 5: "the established CKM G1 is an estimation of the ground-truth CKM") and is evaluated by MAE. Trajectory and transmit power are then designed by SCA and fractional programming (pp. 6-9), which are not learned, so the learned method does not perform the power control of area 6. If the reviewer counts the CKM-based power design as the learned problem, area 6 wins by priority and q3 becomes 0, since the rate comparisons (Schemes II and III, p. 12) have no learned baseline. System check: no antenna numbers are stated and the SINR uses a scalar channel power gain (p. 3), so the links are effectively single-antenna with no RIS; the work passes only through the clause that OTFS and NTN works admit single-antenna links, because the links are aerial (UAV to ground BS). If the reviewer limits that clause to works of areas 4 and 6, the reason would be system (p. 3). q1 and q5: the radio map dataset [24] of central Shanghai is public and called measured, while the 3D city map comes from OpenStreetMap (p. 10, footnote 2), so the reviewer should confirm whether the gains are measured or ray-traced. Carrier frequency not stated.
